solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slow Latin number: a bit of a dog's dinner all round

indicators.note: the bone is placed all round the number, enclosing it

parts.words: a bit of a dog's dinner
parts.note: a bone is a piece of food a dog gets
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sluggish speaker of Latin numbers, with a messy dog's dinner thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's dinner' tempts as slang for a mess, but here it is literal: a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow-like in the sense of dull and sluggish, slow-witted and placid.

clue.text: Roll up note with text for religious ceremonies

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means sitting above, so the roll comes first

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
SMS is a text message service

explanation.surface: Instructions to roll up a note with some text, for church services.
explanation.walkthrough: A BAP is a British bread roll. The blogger thought 'up' an error, but in a down clue it can place BAP on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian rites of initiation using water, a kind of religious ritual.

clue.text: Taking time out, cross bay

indicators.note: taking with out means removing the time abbreviation from the cross
out completes taking out, signalling removal

parts.note: you vote by putting a cross on a ballot

explanation.surface: Taking a break and crossing a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: A VOE is a small bay or creek in Orkney and Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shetland and Orkney word for a small inlet or creek in the coast.

clue.text: Screen: a utility for displaying marine life

indicators.note: displaying shows the letters set out within the words screen a utility

explanation.surface: A screen is a useful thing for showing off sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelled cephalopod molluscs of the ocean, examples of sea creatures.

clue.text: Unusual jade ball dress for Arab lady

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of jade ball come in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: An odd jade-coloured ball gown chosen for a woman from Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose hooded cloak worn in North Africa and the Arab world, by women as well as men.

clue.text: Old master of the turntable is a good DJ who we upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.words: is a good DJ who we

explanation.surface: A disc jockey on the turntables upset by a lowly critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turntable' suggests a DJ's decks, but it is the potter's wheel; Wedgwood was the great 18th-century English potter.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter throwing clay works at a revolving wheel, so the master potter was a master of it.

clue.text: Irish city council finally does live stream

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of council

parts.note: is means exists, does live
a burn is a Scottish stream

explanation.surface: An Irish city council finally lets a stream flow through town.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN is the Scots and northern English word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Northern Ireland, in County Antrim near Belfast.

clue.text: Being in two minds about girl's character

indicators.note: about means going round, so the character surrounds the girl

parts.note: ambience is the character or atmosphere of a place
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Undecided about a girl's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed feelings, uncertainty that pulls a person two ways.

clue.text: Black lining on the ball and chain

indicators.note: lining puts the black abbreviation inside, like a lining

parts.note: being on the ball is being alert
B is black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A prisoner's black-lined ball and chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball and chain' sets up a prisoner's shackle; an albert is a watch chain, named after Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch chain worn across a waistcoat, called after Queen Victoria's consort.

clue.text: Bound to tangle long hair that one's lying on?

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring
to mat is to tangle into a mass
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Destined to tangle someone's long hair while they lie on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'certain to'; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's sprung base is the thing a sleeper lies on.

clue.text: Assumes cheerful attitude amongst journalists

indicators.note: amongst places the cheerful attitude in the middle of the journalists

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively
up means in good spirits
a pose is a stance or attitude struck

explanation.surface: Someone takes for granted they can keep a cheerful face among reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To presuppose is to take something for granted beforehand, i.e. to assume it.

clue.text: What's Auntie briefly fastened around one?

definitions.text: What's Auntie briefly fastened around one?

indicators.note: fastened around puts the shortened name either side of the one
briefly means the name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A riddle about what the BBC, nicknamed Auntie, might tie round someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a baby's protective cloth is what gets fastened around one at mealtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A bib is the cloth tied round a child's neck to protect clothing while eating.

clue.text: Represents Post Impressionism's first religious sect

parts.note: one thing represents another when it is that thing, so is
post and mail are both letters delivered

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Impressionism's

explanation.surface: An art-historical claim that Post-Impressionism stands for a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post Impressionism' reads as the art movement; the words split into post (mail) and the first letter of Impressionism.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of Shia Islam that follows the Aga Khan, a recognised religious community.

clue.text: Drama once commentator's been absent from second cup tie?

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so the words are said out loud

parts.words: been absent from second cup tie
parts.note: to miss a replay, a second cup match after a draw

explanation.surface: A football pundit wonders where they were for the cup replay.
explanation.walkthrough: In English football a drawn cup tie is played again as a REPLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval play dramatising Bible stories, a form of theatre from long ago.

clue.text: One going with a bow, perhaps, far from steady

parts.note: one is the article a
an archer keeps arrows in a quiver, which goes with a bow

explanation.surface: An archer's companion, or a performer taking a bow, unable to keep still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests a curtsey or a violin, but it is the archer's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling or shaking all over, hardly what anyone would call steady.

clue.text: Potter's creation: wide gem, strikingly unusual

indicators.note: unusual tells us the gathered letters appear in an odd, rearranged order

parts.note: W is a wide in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A wide gem with a strikingly unusual look, seemingly fashioned by a potter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of ceramics; it is Beatrix Potter, the children's author.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedgehog washerwoman of Beatrix Potter's tales, one of the author's famous characters.

clue.text: Recites nothing dreadfully obscure

indicators.note: dreadfully means badly done, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone recites nothing but dreadfully obscure verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood only by a select few, abstruse and arcane.

clue.text: Poem from a new father overwhelmed by son: one entering the world

indicators.note: entering puts everything before it inside the planet's name

parts.note: Venus is a world in the sense of a planet

indicators.note: overwhelmed by puts the father and the rest inside the son's letters, swamped by them

parts.note: taken as written
dad is father
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A proud new father is outdone by a newborn son entering the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The world' reads as Earth, but a planet is a world too, so it names the goddess's planet; 'entering' does its work on everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative poem by Shakespeare about the goddess of love and the youth she desires.

clue.text: Left order to follow superior?

indicators.note: to follow puts the order word after the superior letter

parts.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U
to order is to tidy, neaten

explanation.surface: A command to obey one's superior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction; it means remaining on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left over has not been eaten.

clue.text: Adversely affect cases by not behaving properly?

indicators.note: cases means holds within, so the affect word encloses by

parts.note: to dent is to damage or harm
via means by way of

explanation.surface: Legal cases spoiled by someone's improper conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like a noun for lawsuits; it is a verb, encasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Departing from the accepted norms of conduct, aberrant.

clue.text: One wearing fleece, good for this sport?

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the fleece goes round the one

parts.note: a fleece is the skin of a sheep
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Is a fleece good to wear for winter sport?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' tempts as a jacket; here it is an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Downhill or cross-country on snow, a sport in which a fleece jacket is good wear.

clue.text: One entering Yale, maybe, established ties with US town

indicators.note: ties means the established abbreviation is joined on next to the with letter

parts.note: a key enters a Yale lock, Yale being a lock brand

explanation.surface: A student newly entering Yale University, with established connections to an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale looks like the university, but it is the lock maker; what enters a lock is a key.
explanation.definitionFit: A city at the southern tip of the Florida Keys, an American settlement.

clue.text: Unconventional view's at least straight

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unconventional opinion is, at the very least, honest and straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At least straight' looks like 'anyway honest'; read as 'least straight' it is the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: The most curved or undulating, the superlative opposite of straight.

clue.text: State one's going to with complaint

definitions.meaning: a state, as in a poor state of health, being sick
the contraction of I will, as in one is going to

explanation.surface: Someone says they are going to lodge a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick describes a poor state of health; with apostrophe it is I will; and someone ailing has a complaint.

clue.text: One dry summer on odd parts of the Med

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y
odd parts of takes the first, third and fifth letters of the Med

parts.note: a summer is someone who sums, an adder-up of figures

explanation.surface: A dry summer holiday spent on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is the season on the surface; here it is one who sums. 'Dry' means alcohol-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from alcohol is described as dry.

clue.text: Great deal you'll find at sale?

definitions.meaning: an item at an auction, numbered for bidding

explanation.surface: A bargain in the sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty means a large amount; and auction items are offered one numbered piece at a time.

clue.text: S American chap with an effortlessness when speaking

parts.note: a guy is a chap, a man

indicators.note: when speaking means the following word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: ease is effortlessness

explanation.surface: A South American man who talks with fluent ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Guyana, a country on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Fixed problem with reception?

definitions.meaning: crackling interference on a radio or TV signal

explanation.surface: Was the poor TV signal sorted?
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary things are unmoving; and crackle on a broadcast is atmospheric interference.
